transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that brought you in today?
I’ve just been… foggy, I suppose. I keep mixing up simple things — appointment times, exhibit dates, which volunteer I already called. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with your memory and organization?
About four months, I think. It started around when the water damage happened and we had to get into the remodel. Since then it’s been harder to keep things straight.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking or memory besides mixing up appointments and dates? For example, trouble finding words, getting lost, or making decisions?
Mostly just that foggy feeling. I get turned around with simple things I should keep straight — times, dates for the exhibits, whether I’ve already called someone. It’s embarrassing.
Have you had any trouble finding the right words when speaking, felt confused about places or directions, or noticed difficulty making decisions?
Not so much words or directions, no. It’s more that my head feels foggy, and I mix up ordinary things — appointment times, exhibit dates, whether I already called a volunteer. That sort of thing.
Have you ever had trouble finding the right word when speaking, even if just momentarily?
Not really. I mean, maybe once in a while like anyone, but I haven’t noticed that being a problem.
Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts or perceptions, like hearing voices that others don’t hear or believing something strongly that others don’t share?
I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or anything like that… and I can’t think of beliefs like that, no.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to make decisions or judgments, even small ones, like what to wear or what to cook for dinner?

A little, yes. Mostly it’s this foggy feeling… I get mixed up with simple things, like appointment times or exhibit dates, or whether I already called someone. It makes deciding things feel harder sometimes.
Have you had trouble planning or organizing tasks, or getting started on things you need to do?
Yes… a bit. It’s more like my head feels foggy, and then I mix up simple things—appointments, dates for exhibits, or who I already called. So getting organized can take me longer than it should.
Can you tell me if you've had more trouble than before with things like following a recipe, keeping track of bills, or handling money?

Not so much with bills or money… I don’t really know. It’s more that my head feels foggy, and I mix up little things—appointment times, exhibit dates, or which volunteer I already called. That’s the sort of thing that brought me in.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling more tired than usual?
Yes… I guess I’ve lost interest in things. My watercolors, my tomato plants… even watching the cardinals out back. Line dancing too. They’re all still there, but I just… can’t seem to care much.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you're not doing much?
Yes… I do feel tired. I can sleep and still wake up tired. Sometimes just washing up and making breakfast is enough that I need to sit down again.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure or interest in activities like your watercolors, gardening, watching birds, or line dancing?
Yes… I have. Those things I used to love—my watercolors, the tomato plants, line dancing, watching the cardinals out back—they’re still there, but I just… can’t seem to care about them much anymore.
Can you describe how your thinking or memory is different now compared to six months ago, especially when it comes to handling everyday tasks or thinking clearly?

It’s… foggier, I guess. Six months ago I could keep track of things better. Now I mix up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, who I already called for volunteering. It’s embarrassing, so I try not to talk about it much.
Can you tell me if you’ve had increasing difficulty with tasks that used to be routine for you, like following instructions, managing your schedule, or remembering why you walked into a room?
Yes… it’s been harder. Mostly my head feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and whether I already called someone for volunteering. It’s… frustrating.

Has this foggy feeling and trouble keeping track of things ever gotten to the point where you couldn’t manage your usual responsibilities without help, like handling your schedule or remembering important commitments?

Yes… I suppose it has. I’ve missed doctor visits, and I’ve gotten the senior center schedule all mixed up. My husband’s had to help with the calls and calendars… and even decisions about repairs that I used to handle myself. It’s hard to admit that.
Have you ever experienced any strange sensations or perceptions, like seeing, hearing, or feeling things that others around you don’t seem to notice?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t noticed anything like that. Sometimes I’m just unsure of myself, but not seeing or hearing things, as far as I can tell.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything, even things you used to really enjoy?
Yes… I have. The things I used to enjoy—my watercolors, the tomato plants, even line dancing—mostly just sit there now. I’ll look out at the cardinals in the yard and… I just can’t seem to care much.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, like sleeping more or less than usual, or changes in your weight?
My appetite’s not been very good. Most days I just pick at some toast or soup… food doesn’t sound like much. And, well, my skirts are looser lately, though I haven’t been trying to lose weight.
Have you ever believed something strongly that others around you don’t seem to share, even when they’ve tried to tell you otherwise?

I suppose… yes, maybe. There was a time I really felt like I was the only one who could make our senior center into something special—something people from all over town would come see. Other folks didn’t quite see it that way.
